---
title: "Standardized-evidence flags in a league"
subtitle: "3.4 · a simulated league after the postrank theory book, ch. 23"
description: "Pairwise directions and posterior risk of a thirty-unit flag report."
---

Grouping thirty units by standardized distance from the league mean treats an estimated reference as fixed and can rank precise lower estimates above noisy higher ones.

```{=html}

```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **League, cutoff 1.96.** Groups of 6, 22 and 2 state 188 of 435 pairs (E/N = .130, risk .170, 20 reversals, max error .649).
- **Same flags, flat prior.** The same 188 pairs are evaluated under flat-prior normals around the estimates.
- **League, cutoff 2.576.** Shrinks the outer groups and updates matrix blocks.
- **Same report, τ .10.** Keeps 188 stated pairs while lowering all-withheld risk to τ = .10.

<details>
<summary>Reversals and individual comparison errors</summary>

At cutoff 1.96, 20 stated directions reverse the order of the estimates, and the largest error probability is
.649 even though E/N lies below τ. Both matrix axes follow decreasing estimates; use the arrow keys, pointer, or Data table to inspect any pair.

</details>

Standalone: [flags-in-the-league](../../embed/flags-in-the-league.html), for example `?crit=1.96&prior=teaching&tau=.10`.
